chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from 'Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had cupping done, and a slave of the Banu Bayadah did cupping on him, and he gave him (payment). And if it were forbidden, he would not have given him. So when he was finished, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Where is the blood?' He said, 'I drank it, O Messenger of Allah.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It was not befitting for you to do that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made it a barrier for you from the Fire, so do not repeat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying for cupping and the permissibility of the cupper drinking the blood?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility of *ujrah* (wage) for cupping by citing the Prophet’s payment to a slave, a key argument in Shia jurisprudence against those who view it merely as a charitable act. The narrative further highlights the spiritual significance of the procedure, where the Prophet instructs the cupper to consume the blood, declaring it a 'barrier from the Fire,' thereby linking physical purification with eschatological reward.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ahmad Bin Al nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had cupping done, and it was a slave of the Clan of Bayaza who did cupping on him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> gave him (payment), and had it been Prohibited, he<sup>saww</sup> would not have given it. So when he was free, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Where is the blood?’ He said, ‘I drank it, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It was not befitting for you that you should do that, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Made a barrier for you from the Fire, but do not repeat’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shamir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, did use cupping services. A Mawla’ (slave) of banu Bayada performed cupping service for the Messenger of Allah and paid for such services. Had it been unlawful he would not pay for it. When cupping was complete the Messenger of Allah asked, ‘Where is the blood?’ He (the slave) replied, ‘I drank it, O Messenger of Allah.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘You should not have done so. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made it a curtain between you and the fire but do not do it again.’”
